meaning: DOC-03: the machine-readable findings register. Each finding has its ID, severity, the group and area it was found in, the revision it was found against, its text (or its finding, evidence, failure scenario, recommendation and effort), its status and, where the register held one, its resolution. tools/findings-register.mjs validates it and writes the open view (FINDINGS.md) and the closed view (FINDINGS-CLOSED.md); npm run docs:index:check fails when either differs. Converted on 2026-10-24 from the hand-written FINDINGS.md, whose text it keeps.

notes.text:
Additional investigations, including policy races, malformed report envelopes, cumulative request budgets, resumed
lineage and health-check concurrency, are recorded separately in the comprehensive review. They are not labelled
as reproduced defects.

**Batch 151 improvement:** the standalone privacy policy now supplies all eight sections in Arabic
with complete public no-script language routes and current-language website links. Original English
policy content, dates, scopes and destinations remain. This closes the recorded English-only policy
scope item; broader editorial/assistive/deployed acceptance remains separate. See [Arabic privacy delivery and boundaries](../records/DELIVERY-2026-10-04-ARABIC-PRIVACY.md).

**Batch 152 capability improvement:** selected WooCommerce child sources and explicit reviewed Meta
groups were unsupported in two synthetic feature baselines. A bounded source union, repeated parent
membership/child/currency evidence, literal source values and visibly reviewed titles now support
that selected workflow. Missing/unsupported fields remain blockers, no native child name is invented
and no group/full-inventory/live acceptance is inferred. See [evidence and remaining scope](../records/DELIVERY-2026-10-04-WOOCOMMERCE-VARIATIONS.md).

**Batch 153 capability/workflow improvement:** two synthetic feature baselines refused optional Meta
groups in canonical and supplier CSV paths, and two actual selected WooCommerce views retained
unrelated CSV layout controls. Exact optional group mapping, destination-bound loaded columns and
scoped source-mode visibility now support that flow while retaining X refusal, original values and
the existing per-product review/receipt/field proof. See [qualification](../records/DELIVERY-2026-10-04-META-GROUP-CSV.md). No live incident is inferred.

**Batch 156 capability improvement:** the four existing guided Google report levels lacked a native
keyword/day dimension. Official v25 keyword_view documentation supports a separate positive Search
criterion report. Exact native identity/text/match type, complete bounded pages and current authority
now qualify local evidence capture, bilingual filtering and optional every-row Excel projection. This
is a new reporting capability, not a claimed prior defect/live incident. See [scope and evidence](../records/DELIVERY-2026-10-05-GOOGLE-KEYWORD-EVIDENCE.md).

**Batch 159 capability improvement:** guided Google evidence lacked a separate campaign/device/day
view. Current official v25 segmentation/field/enum documentation supports it. Exact literal device
categories, campaign resources, bounded current-authority capture, retained filtering and optional
full-row Excel now qualify the selected local workflow. This is a capability extension, not a prior
defect or live incident. See [research and evidence](../records/DELIVERY-2026-10-05-GOOGLE-DEVICE-EVIDENCE.md).

findings.text:
**Batch 65:** F-140 (medium), reproduced against `6bda0ad`: the creative-push controller displayed **Uploaded** for
a durable queued result. The ignored baseline harness uses the original controller; the checked-in regression
in `tests/campaign-localization.test.mjs` verifies the queued label, original-review link, exact source hash and
explicit consent in both languages. Fixed in batch 65; no additional upload is submitted for status recovery.

**Batch 68:** F-141 (medium), reproduced against `680fac7`: measurement/product previews could paint old account
data or errors after form, route or identity changes. A slow file read could send an obsolete preview, an old
preview could still save a local plan, and a late save could redirect a new view. `tests/account-localization.test.mjs`
and an ignored original-controller harness reproduce five scenario groups. Fixed by current-form/result identity,
route/identity generations, sequenced attempts, input invalidation and checks before submission/after each await.
Current errors remain visible; native requests and money semantics are unchanged.

**Batch 69:** F-142 (medium), reproduced against `ac1be5f`: a client deletion confirmation could delete a newly
selected client instead of the client named in the dialog. Client previews/local saves and report-branding responses
could also act on or repaint a newer selection; edits retained approval, and departed callbacks exposed stale errors.
Fixed by capturing the original ID/revision, invalidating selection/form versions, checking route/identity/current
nodes before submission and after awaits, and clearing approval on edits. Nine red/green regressions cover native
request parity, confirmations, previews, saves, refresh feedback and downloads in `tests/client-localization.test.mjs`.
No provider writes are introduced and already submitted local writes are not repeated.

**Batch 70:** F-143 (medium), reproduced against `ef551fa`: capture discovery/results did not fence identity and
edited measurement settings; completeness remained approved after edits. Older scenario results/errors could reach
a newer form and stale allocation callbacks could submit/download or expose errors. Fixed with per-form sequences,
current identity/view/node checks, completeness invalidation and scoped callbacks. Nine original-controller red/green
tests in `tests/evidence-localization.test.mjs` cover these cases, current errors, English/Arabic request equality and
HTML artifact language/direction. Already submitted retained-evidence writes are not automatically repeated.

**Batch 72:** F-144 (medium), reproduced against `b77e7cb`: the LinkedIn generic paginator interpreted normal
analytics metadata without `paging.total` as a next page, synthesized an invalid offset and failed with
`PAGINATION_LOOP`. Analytics now has a separate completion check: one bounded response, no invented page, and
explicit refusal of continuation metadata or the provider element ceiling. Other finders retain cursor/offset
pagination. The native/service regression is in `tests/linkedin-evidence-presets.test.mjs`; this also covers the
new guided evidence presets' account currency, native UTC grain, exact IDs, missing metrics and revocation.

**Batch 73:** F-145 (medium), reproduced against `588b0b3`: LinkedIn Overview accepted empty analytics, a next-page
link and wrong-period rows as complete. Its native collector also accepted duplicate campaigns (the downstream
overview already rejected duplicate campaign rows). Unverified conversion-rule attribution was labelled `provider
configured`, allowing an otherwise efficient campaign to pass scale guidance. Native account/currency, campaign
pivot, exact period and completion checks now precede acceptance; attribution remains `unknown`. Calendar errors
stay partial, complete-only delivery remains blocked, and old LinkedIn collection state requires a new snapshot
without modifying checkpoints. Six red/green cases are in `tests/linkedin-overview-evidence.test.mjs`.

**Batch 74:** F-146 (medium), reproduced against `0f4d615`: matching caller-supplied totals rendered a `verified`
badge although their account, dates, currency, timezone and attribution had not been checked. Manual comparisons
now explicitly mean numerical agreement only. Retained-source comparisons require compatible declared semantics
and native grain, preserve both source hashes and still do not claim independent provider verification.

F-147 (medium): older analysis/reconciliation responses and failures could survive edited forms or replace newer
results; report discovery/get callbacks could cross an identity change. Current form/attempt/selection/view/identity
guards suppress departed results/errors while retaining current failures. Ten new tests were observed red; two
additional boundary tests cover authority and exact tolerances. The focused 14-test group passes.

**Batch 76:** F-148 (medium), visually reproduced against `1281bd9`: PDFKit's word-cached default layout
shaped Arabic words without ordering the complete Arabic phrase, so client names and titles read in the wrong order.
Unicode bidirectional runs now preserve logical Arabic input for shaping, Latin IDs/decimals and punctuation.
Dates and native label/value groups are isolated; long text wraps by graphemes and logical words. A stress render
also caught reversed parentheses during implementation; a red regression preceded correction against the pinned
library's actual levels-array API. English/Arabic standard PDFs and a long mixed-script compact PDF were rendered
and every page inspected. This is local visual evidence, not PDF/UA or independent Arabic editorial certification.

**Batch 77:** F-149 (medium), reproduced in the shared page-controller harness against `d03fc32`: a pending
`workPageLoader` response still painted after `identityGeneration` changed without a route-generation change.
The loader tracked route/request/DOM lifetime but omitted identity. It now checks all four and refuses a departed
handler before it sends another request. The new red/green case is in `tests/operations-browser.test.mjs`.
This demonstrates a controller isolation defect; it does not establish an observed deployed cross-user incident.

**Batch 79:** F-150 (medium), reproduced against `b24576c`: legacy query rebinding left a linked schedule
attached to the old workbook and active; another probe moved a granted query out of a mixed-access source
association. Both associations now require current complete query access, and all schedules move/pause atomically.
Reviewed website/MCP moves additionally bind the query, both associations, their memberships and schedules to
the displayed versions. Original jobs are unchanged; this is local fixture evidence, not a deployed incident.

**Batch 81:** F-151 (medium), reproduced against `b6edd65`: departed portfolio handlers could initiate new
reads after route/identity changes or a detached view. A pre-request guard now checks current form/view/route/identity;
existing late-response fencing remains. The red/green case is in `tests/portfolio-ui.test.mjs`. This establishes a
controller defect, not an observed deployed cross-user disclosure; backend account checks remain independent.

**Batch 82:** F-152 (high), reproduced against `c7a086c` (the history implementation was unchanged from
`b6edd65`): a reader granted account 100 received account 200 request bodies/receipts through MCP history. Website
Activity used the same unscoped full-event projection. Both now share a bounded metadata allowlist, current-account
checks for ordinary members, own-event handling for unscoped events, owner-only workspace-wide metadata and
independently scoped diagnostic items. No role receives raw request/outcome/receipt fields. Five red/green backend
cases plus authenticated HTTP, SDK and UI tests cover access, revocation, pagination and preserved native diagnostics.
The audit chain is unchanged; no deployed disclosure is asserted.

**Batch 86:** F-153 (medium), reproduced against `20ef776`: Google portfolio accepted edited cursors and
continued after credentials changed between requests, passed through unselected provider fields, and accepted
invalid account/resource identities and unsafe integer money. Native request guards already rejected in-flight
authorization changes. `src/google-portfolio.ts` now signs and expires authorization-bound cursors, validates exact
account/parent/resource chains and money, projects selected metadata, and disables automatic native continuation.
Eight backend red cases plus the real-SDK cursor case are fixed; one existing native guard case remains green.
An omitted empty collection additionally requires its exact requested native field mask. Tests prove local integrity
and minimization defects, not a live disclosure. See [delivery evidence](../records/DELIVERY-2026-10-02-GOOGLE-PORTFOLIO.md).

findings.finding: Nothing showed an MCP outage. On 2026-09-24 every call, even the offline help, returned "Connection closed" while the owner's app showed AMCP as connected. `/healthz` answered `up` whatever the state; refusals before MCP (token, origin, size, parse, internal) came back in a shape MCP clients cannot read, which they report as a closed connection; nothing was logged; Node's 5-second keep-alive sat behind a proxy. Any browser `Origin` other than AMCP's own is refused, so a client that sends one fails every call while its OAuth stays connected, a plausible cause that production logs could confirm
findings.recommendation: A health check that runs the database and MCP; JSON-RPC refusals that name their reason; a log line per refusal; a keep-alive longer than proxy idle timeouts; an owner-controlled origin allowlist
findings.resolution: fixed (batch 28; the origin allowlist is empty by default, and whether to list `https://claude.ai` is the owner's decision)

findings.finding: Plan refusals asked for the wrong thing. `recover_step` demanded confirmation before checking the step could be recovered at all ("Confirm recovery of the failed step.", then refused anyway); `cancel` said "Confirm cancellation." without naming `confirmed`; a plan step's `RECOVERY_NOT_SAFE` carried the media-upload remedy; `amcp_workspace check` answered `requirements.currency` with "Unsupported arguments or request too large"

findings.finding: A step whose read-back disagreed the same way every time had no exit: verification said inconclusive and pointed back to itself, `reconcile_step` returned the same, `recover_step` refused, and only cancelling the plan remained (the owner's 25 September test). findings.recommendation: Classify a stable disagreement as a mismatch with its diff; an audited, confirmed acceptance of the observed state
findings.resolution: fixed (batch 29, Snapchat S5: when every read of two verification rounds returns the same differing state, the result is `VERIFICATION_MISMATCH` with a per-field diff and the observed `actual_hash`; one round is not enough, so a slow propagation is not called a mismatch. No read is suggested when another cannot change the answer. `reconcile_step` with `accept_observed: true` and the hash reads once more, refuses a state that moved (`STATE_CHANGED`, with the new hash), and otherwise marks the step `verified_with_acceptance` with an audit entry, sending nothing; dependants continue, and a mismatch holds only its dependants)

findings.finding: A reviewed Google Ads mutation or Snapchat batch takes at most 25 records, so the owner's 84 negative keywords needed four separate reviews and approvals. Reported by the owner
findings.recommendation: Split longer lists into parts behind one approval, keeping every per-part control
findings.resolution: fixed (batch 29, owner item 4: up to 1,000 records become one review of parts of 25 (`group: true`); each part keeps its own state reads, hash, idempotency key, spending check and read-back; execution is approved once, checks every part's review window first, stops at the first part that fails and never runs a stopped group again; plans and preflight treat the list as one step)

findings.finding: A campaign plan needed one approval per step: the owner's 19-step Google build took 19 prepare-and-execute rounds, each asking the user again
findings.recommendation: Approve the plan once, then run it under that approval without loosening any per-step control
findings.resolution: fixed (batch 29, owner item 5: `approve` shows every step's action, account, money and status fields; the user's approval is recorded with the plan's hash and audited; `run` prepares and executes every step under it, each still a frozen, state-checked, read-back review with its own idempotency key; spending needs the approval's own acknowledgement; owner cap overrides, creative edits, failures and mismatches still stop for a person; amending a step voids the approval. Not all-or-nothing: Google's atomic multi-resource mutate has no reviewed family yet, so completed steps stay, as created and paused)

findings.finding: Rebuilding an existing campaign meant writing every step by hand; the owner's rebuild would have been one command with a clone. Reported by the owner (item 10)
findings.recommendation: Build a draft plan from the source campaign, with a spec's changes, and run it like any plan
findings.resolution: fixed (batch 29, owner item 10: `amcp_campaign clone` reads a Google Search campaign or a Snapchat campaign through the account's own reads and returns a draft plan under a new name; only fields AMCP already sends on create are copied and `not_copied` lists the rest; `changes.set` sets fields by JSON pointer (never the action or a `$ref`) and `changes.drop` leaves steps out with their dependants; the copy starts PAUSED; nothing is sent until the plan is approved and run, each step still reviewed. Other campaign types and platforms are refused with `CLONE_UNSUPPORTED`)

findings.finding: On Snapchat, Meta and TikTok every new ad squad, ad set, ad group and ad had to start paused even under a paused campaign, so a build needed a second reviewed activation per child that protected nothing; Google's children were already covered (F-103)
findings.recommendation: Decide by the parents' status the review already reads; the owner approved the recommendation on 2026-09-29
findings.resolution: fixed (batch 30, the owner's decision 2: a child may start active when the review reads its parent as paused, and an ad also when its parent serves but the campaign that parent names is paused, which the review then reads too; checked at prepare and at execute; `PARENT_SERVING` names the statuses; campaigns still start paused and an owner policy with `allow_activation: false` still refuses any active create. The Snapchat clone keeps each squad's and ad's status and the Meta recipe creates its ad set and ad active under the paused campaign)

findings.finding: A Google build approved once still ran as separate requests, so a failure part-way left the earlier resources in place; the owner asked for all or nothing (item 5)
findings.recommendation: Review Google's multi-resource mutate as its own family
findings.resolution: fixed (batch 30, the owner's decision 1: `googleAds:mutate` with up to 1,000 creates of six resource types is one reviewed write that Google applies completely or not at all; temporary names only where the contract allows; each operation checked as its own service would; existing parents read; paused-parent rules applied to the build's own records; spend confirmation, activation policy and budget caps apply; every created resource read back. A Google clone is one such build by default. Record: `docs/implementation/GOOGLE-ATOMIC-BUILDS-2026-09-29.md`)

findings.finding: A Google build that Google refused outright was recorded as an uncertain outcome, so its plan could only be cancelled although the pinned contract says a refused build applied nothing
findings.recommendation: Let a definitive refusal of an all-or-nothing build be amended under a new key; keep every other post-submission failure as it is
findings.resolution: fixed (batch 30, the owner's decision 5: a `googleAds:mutate` build with `partial_failure` false refused with HTTP 400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 412 or 422 is amended with `recover_step` and reviewed again under a new key, audited as `campaign_step_recovered_after_rejection`; its old key stays uncertain and is never sent again. A lost response, a timeout, an HTTP 5xx, and every refusal of other families still stop the plan: their documentation does not establish that nothing was applied. Batch 33 checked Snapchat, Meta and TikTok: Snapchat documents multi-record requests as not atomic, Meta's error guide is silent, TikTok's pages are unreadable here; see ROADMAP P6)

findings.finding: Clone covered only Google Search and Snapchat, so a TikTok or LinkedIn rebuild still meant writing every step by hand; LinkedIn's children could not reference a parent at all, because LinkedIn returns a new ID only as a bare number in a header while a child names its parent by URN
findings.recommendation: Clone both from the account's own reads, with only the fields in the vendors' own create schemas; let a reference build a LinkedIn URN from a numeric ID, and nothing else
findings.resolution: fixed (batch 31: a TikTok campaign, its ad groups and their ads, one ad per step, with only the fields of TikTok's official create models, the campaign DISABLE and its children keeping their status; a LinkedIn campaign group, its campaigns and their creatives, only the writable fields of the li-lms-2026-05 schemas, every entity PAUSED. A plan reference may carry `prefix`, accepted only as `urn:li:<type>:` and only over a bare numeric ID, otherwise `INVALID_REFERENCE` before anything is sent; preflight lists such fields as deferred like any reference. Each cloned entity is still reviewed under today's rules)

findings.finding: LinkedIn's search and criteria finders page by cursor (`metadata.nextPageToken`, sent back as `pageToken`), but AMCP followed LinkedIn pages only by `paging.total`, so `aggregate_pages` stopped after the first page and returned it as complete; and the workspace's creative read used a `q=search` finder the versioned creatives API does not document (it has `q=criteria`), or a bare collection read

findings.resolution: fixed (batch 31: the cursor is followed until a page has none; a cursor on a read paged by offset, a malformed cursor or a repeated one is refused; offset finders still page by `paging.total`; the state-read check that refuses paginated before-state now also sees LinkedIn's cursor. `fetch_ads` reads creatives with `q=criteria`, `campaigns: List(urn)` when a campaign is named, `X-RestLi-Method: FINDER` and pages of at most 100. Source: Microsoft Learn "Create and Manage Creatives", li-lms-2026-05, read 2026-09-29)

findings.finding: Meta's v26.0 changelog refuses the Instagram Explore placement and poll components (poll on every version from 2026-10-27), requires an explicit Advantage+ Audience choice for Housing, Employment and Financial ad sets with relaxable targeting, and defaults creatives of advertisers with a shop to `WEBSITE_AND_SHOP`. findings.resolution: fixed (batch 33: `META_PLACEMENT_UNAVAILABLE`, `META_POLL_UNAVAILABLE` and `META_ADVANTAGE_AUDIENCE_REQUIRED`; the review of a new creative or an ad with an inline creative without a destination carries `creative_impact.warning`; the creative contract accepts `destination_spec: {destination_type: WEBSITE_AND_SHOP_OPT_OUT}` and no other destination; `tests/meta-v26-rules.test.mjs`. findings.finding: The website named every LinkedIn ad account "LinkedIn Ads <id>", a name no read returned, and the media push, ad previews and spending policy pickers showed accounts by ID only

findings.text:
**Batch 91:** F-154 (medium), reproduced against `b264bca`: TikTok integrated aggregation accepted missing
completion metadata, changing totals and overlapping dimension tuples as complete. A saved Overview without
page_info retained successful metrics. Strict native page counts, stable totals and unique requested-dimensional
tuples now stop those reports before metric retention. Sole-source failure remains a failed report with scoped
diagnostics. Seven red/green regressions include native pagination and saved Overview jobs. This is local integrity
evidence, not an assertion of observed incorrect deployed reporting. See [delivery evidence](../records/DELIVERY-2026-10-02-TIKTOK-REPORT-COMPLETION.md).

**Batch 94:** F-155 (medium), reproduced in full root regression on the batch-93 backup code: Windows EPERM
while removing backup staging replaced BACKUP_AUDIT_FAILED with a raw filesystem exception. Cleanup now yields
between six bounded attempts and reports a persistent failure with the original error code, known staging path
and operation-completed flag, preserving a restore already published. Two injected regressions were red before
repair; post-publication cleanup is covered separately. No specific OS lock holder or universal lock cure is claimed.
See [delivery evidence](../records/DELIVERY-2026-10-02-GTM-CONSENT.md).

**Batch 95:** F-156 (medium), reproduced against the previous guided Google capture: foreign customer/currency/timezone,
out-of-window dates, duplicate campaign/day rows and missing campaign identity were accepted and saved. Duplicate rows
doubled spend in the synthetic probe. Guided presets now verify customer metadata before/after, complete native counts,
current authority, exact hierarchy/resource identity and unique requested date grain. Ads/search terms preserve full
native resource identity. Nine red/green cases plus a new SDK journey passed; no incorrect live result is asserted.
See [delivery evidence](../records/DELIVERY-2026-10-02-GOOGLE-EVIDENCE-INTEGRITY.md).

**Batch 98:** F-157 (medium), reproduced against the prior LinkedIn guided capture: credential/scope changes during native
reads still allowed retention, account identity arrays were coerced to matching strings, and the single initial account
read could not detect subsequent currency/identity changes. Guided capture now binds every await to current authorization,
requires exact account identity, brackets a complete bounded analytics response with account checks and keeps all source
references. Five backend cases and one bilingual UI case were observed red; no incorrect live result is asserted.
See [delivery evidence](../records/DELIVERY-2026-10-02-LINKEDIN-EVIDENCE-INTEGRITY.md).

**Batch 100:** F-158 (medium), reproduced in a synthetic reviewed Google negative-keyword journey: after an initial
SPEND_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED refusal, a successfully acknowledged, executed and verified step still exposed the old
error. Accepted native execution now clears that current-step diagnostic; original attempt evidence and receipt
recovery remain intact. The observed red assertion and accepted-retry/replay checks passed.
See [delivery evidence](../records/DELIVERY-2026-10-02-SEARCH-EXCLUSION-PLANS.md).

**Batch 102:** F-159 (low), reproduced by directly importing the capability module in a fresh Node process: a circular
dependency caused an eager scope-binding copy in the workspace module to access an uninitialized export. A live import
alias preserves the same scope policy and allows that entry order. Normal service-first startup already worked; no
deployed outage is asserted. The observed red subprocess regression now passes.
See [delivery evidence](../records/DELIVERY-2026-10-02-GOOGLE-CLICKS-RECIPE.md).

**Batch 104:** F-160 (high): eight synthetic cases accepted incomplete, malformed or mismatched Meta catalog evidence, including false price verification from another product ID. Exact native identities, complete bounded product pages and receipt-bound price/sale-price proof now refuse those cases. Thirty catalog checks and the full local suite pass; no live incident is asserted. See [delivery evidence](../records/DELIVERY-2026-10-03-CATALOG-EVIDENCE.md).

**Batch 105:** F-161 (medium): existing campaign preflight accepted foreign/coerced account identity or unfinished native paging as currency evidence. Three observed red cases now require validated complete state and exact scalar identity before evidence retention (`src/campaign-preflight.ts:163`).

F-162 (medium): delayed campaign inspections/errors and targeting results/errors overwrote changed form/account/query state; four observed red races now discard obsolete responses (`web/campaign-recipes.js:196`, `web/campaign-recipes.js:253`). No incorrect live result is asserted. See [delivery evidence](../records/DELIVERY-2026-10-03-RECIPE-ELIGIBILITY.md).

**Batch 106:** F-163 (high): explicit failed Snapchat collection/account/entity wrappers and foreign/coerced owner identities were accepted as cached ownership evidence. Six synthetic cases were observed red, including organization ownership and renewal beyond the original expiry. `src/scope.ts:503` now ignores failed observations and mismatched owner identities; three fake-transport service journeys prove they cannot authorize a later global stats request. Qualified account-edge observations retain existing behavior and TTL. No live incident is asserted. See [delivery evidence](../records/DELIVERY-2026-10-03-SNAPCHAT-SQUAD-EVIDENCE.md).

**Batch 107:** F-164 (high): an existing Snapchat nested-update review omitted native ad-squad delivery mode from its frozen state. A synthetic race after allocation validation submitted one PATCH under a changed delivery mode. `src/snapchat-nested-updates.ts:540` now retains immutable native delivery context separately from the PUT/PATCH body; drift prevents dispatch and optional native enum shape is checked. No live incident or additional mutable field is asserted. See [delivery evidence](../records/DELIVERY-2026-10-03-SNAPCHAT-ALLOCATION.md).

**Batch 108:** F-165 (low): actual synthetic ad-squad results/draft copy retained campaign and average-daily terminology; Arabic generic translations also inserted campaigns. Selected labels, diagnostics, model unit/parent metadata and draft descriptions now name the qualified native unit.
F-166 (low): Tab from the final confirmation control put focus on BODY with the modal still open; forward/reverse wrapping and listener cleanup now pass red/green and actual browser checks.

F-167 (low): long native IDs at 390 px expanded the RTL page to 435 px, and the global click delegate re-enabled selected controls owned by another controller. Scoped zero-minimum grid tracks, compact named Add/Added controls, wrapping actions, persistent selected state and ownership of delegated disabled state fix the observed cases; document/client width is now 375/375 px. No live incident or full accessibility certification is asserted. See [browser allocation qualification](../records/DELIVERY-2026-10-03-BROWSER-ALLOCATION.md).

**Batch 109:** F-168 (low): Arabic report cards exposed internal metric keys, missing metrics became blank, and newly opened plan rows retained English step-count text. Known labels and step counts are now translated; missing/null stay Unknown and exact zero/decimal values are preserved.

F-169 (low): expanding the original brief's long fingerprint at 390 × 844 widened the RTL document to 534 px. Scoped paragraph/title wrapping restores 375/375 px without truncation. The saved Google/Snapchat proposal now has a readable source-linked bilingual summary while exact native requests, original descriptions and provenance remain intact. No live incident or full accessibility certification is asserted. See [allocation review evidence](../records/DELIVERY-2026-10-03-ALLOCATION-REVIEW.md).
**Batch 111:** F-170 (low): the reusable recipe-default editor omitted the existing Google Maximize Clicks CPC ceiling. The field now preserves its exact text.
F-171 (low): resolved playbook approval preview omitted returned campaign defaults and conversion mappings; both now appear, with readable references and escaped preserved complex JSON.
F-172 (low): UTM labels and the known authored preview explanation remained English in Arabic; their exact first-party text is translated without changing native paths/unknown diagnostics.

F-173 (low): the mobile profile preview widened the document to 540/375 px. Scoped minimum-width/wrapping changes restore 375/375 px in both languages and a 297/297 px conversion table. Red/green regressions and actual synthetic browser observations are in the [delivery record](../records/DELIVERY-2026-10-03-CONVERSION-REFERENCES.md). No live incident or full accessibility certification is asserted.

**Batch 112:** F-174 (medium): owner-only access trusted an identified actor's stale owner membership even after current membership changed to administrator. Current active owner membership is now authoritative; a synthetic red reproduces the old fast path.
F-175 (low): a long recent-source filename widened the actual mobile document to 419/375 px; scoped wrapping restores 375/375 px.

F-176 (low): a connected Cancel control in a closed dialog prevented common focus restoration; a red regression and actual Arabic keyboard check now restore the originating file control. No live misuse or accessibility certification is asserted. The new owner-confirmed encrypted retention feature and its separate source/receipt/backup semantics are documented in [delivery evidence](../records/DELIVERY-2026-10-03-RETAINED-ORIGINALS.md).

A red regression reproduced `CREATIVE_USAGE_REQUIRED`. The scoped path projection now handles SQLite quotes while preserving native resource values. The new Google Ads/Snapchat/standard TikTok joins, SDK revocation and bilingual readable table qualification are in the [delivery record](../records/DELIVERY-2026-10-03-LINKED-AD-PERFORMANCE.md).
